The rules
  • Across an average: the close was on one side of its 50-day or 200-day average at the start of the period and is on the other side at the end.
  • The averages cross: the 50-day average was below the 200-day at the start and is above it at the end (positive), or the reverse (negative).
  • 52-week high or low: a close in the period was above (below) every close of the 252 trading days before it, and the last close is within 3% of it.
  • Heavy volume: a day in the period traded at least twice the average volume of the 50 days before it and closed 2% or more up (positive) or down (negative). US lines only: a venue outside the US shows a part of the trading.
  • These moves are in the line's own currency. A line can be in both lists. A list shows the lines with most to say first, then the largest: the first 5, and the rest behind "more".

How to read this page

  • Weights are given for sleeves only. Inside a sleeve the lines run from the largest to the smallest, and the heatmap draws them the same size.
  • A sleeve's weight and move are rounded to a tenth of a percent, and what it added to a whole basis point (a hundredth of a percent of the book).
  • Every move is in dollars. A euro line's move is its price change and the change in EUR/USD together.
  • Cash is held flat.
  • A line's chart is in the currency of its listing, which is euros for the lines listed in Europe. The watchlist reads that chart, so its moves are in that currency too.
  • Positions are those of Fri 30 Oct 2026; a trade since then is not here.
  • A personal learning project. Nothing here is investment advice.

The rules
  • Across an average: the close was on one side of its 50-day or 200-day average at the start of the period and is on the other side at the end.
  • The averages cross: the 50-day average was below the 200-day at the start and is above it at the end (positive), or the reverse (negative).
  • 52-week high or low: a close in the period was above (below) every close of the 252 trading days before it, and the last close is within 3% of it.
  • Heavy volume: a day in the period traded at least twice the average volume of the 50 days before it and closed 2% or more up (positive) or down (negative). US lines only: a venue outside the US shows a part of the trading.
  • These moves are in the line's own currency. A line can be in both lists. A list shows the lines with most to say first, then the largest: the first 5, and the rest behind "more".

How to read this page

  • The week is today's positions, as if held all week: trades in between are not in it, so it is not the account's return.
  • Weights are given for sleeves only. Inside a sleeve the lines run from the largest to the smallest, and the heatmap draws them the same size.
  • A sleeve's weight and move are rounded to a tenth of a percent, and what it added to a whole basis point (a hundredth of a percent of the book).
  • Every move is in dollars. A euro line's move is its price change and the change in EUR/USD together.
  • Cash is held flat.
  • A line's chart is in the currency of its listing, which is euros for the lines listed in Europe. The watchlist reads that chart, so its moves are in that currency too.
  • Positions are those of Fri 30 Oct 2026; a trade since then is not here.
  • A personal learning project. Nothing here is investment advice.
